messages:
mike_h: alert from infra-bot — na-south2 control plane heartbeat drift detected, auth token fetches failing for ~2m, console 502s. GPU provisioning jobs are piling up. Anyone oncall?
infra-bot: [ALERT] controlplane.heartbeat.drift na-south2 severity=high replicas=3 drift_ms=12000 affected_services=[auth, routing, console] link=https://pager.redwood/INC-2031
oncall_j: I'm on it. Kicking off quick triage — checking apiserver, etcd, and CM sync.
sara_r: grabbing etcd leader/stats now. early look: kv apply latency spiked, txn queue growing. maybe network flaps between controlplane nodes.
priya_ml: GPU provisioning backlog looks like this: 14 pods Pending > 10m, reason: "Failed scheduling: node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector" — suspicious. Also node pool autoscaler shows scaling stalled.
carol_p: console logs show auth proxy returning 502s: 
```
ERROR proxy: upstream disconnected during handshake
context: token fetch failed: 503 service_unavailable
```
tom_ops: can we traffic-shift serving away from na-south2 to na-west2 for critical workloads? we should avoid full failover until controlplane stable. propose 30% shift.
oncall_j: I'll open routing policy change (canary) — route 30% of traffic for model endpoints -> na-west2, TTL 10m, monitor errors. Patching route: 
```
PATCH /v1/routing/policies/traffic-shift
{ "from": "na-south2", "to": "na-west2", "weight": 30, "monitor": "latency+errors" }
```
priya_ml: note: Dedicated GPU pools in na-west2 are on-demand; cost will jump if we keep long. estimate +18% infra spend at 30% traffic. starting a ticket for budget approval.
sara_r: etcd peers show intermittent connection resets between cp-1 and cp-3. grabbing tcpdump and controlplane logs.
oncall_j: tcpdump snippet: 
```
12:34:10.123 IP cp-1 > cp-3: RST, seq 0
12:34:10.124 IP cp-3 > cp-1: RST, seq 0
```
carol_p: rolling the small config push that was in flight earlier might be the trigger — there was a certificate hot-reload patch. I queued a rollback of that config change to eliminate variables.
mike_h: good call, rollback in-progress. keeping canary traffic at 30% while we watch auth success rate.
infra-bot: [ACTION] routing.policy.updated by oncall_j: policy_id=rp-904 weight=30 duration=10m
priya_ml: provisioning backlog reduced to 6 Pending after forcing scheduler resync on autoscaler. command used: `kubectl annotate nodepool na-west2 autoscaler/force-resync=true`
sara_r: after rollback, controlplane heartbeats recovered on cp-3 -> drift down to <300ms, auth token failures dropped. still monitoring for flaps.
oncall_j: will run incremental ramp: 30% -> 60% -> 100% only if no errors for 15m at each step. next step in 12m.
tom_ops: note for postmortem — need playbook update: when controlplane heartbeat drift impacts auth, avoid immediate full failover; prefer gradual routing shift and autoscaler resync. Also add metrics for gpu provisioning queue length to alert earlier.
carol_p: console access restored for most users after rollback. one internal admin session hit stale cert, cleared by restarting auth-proxy pod.
mike_h: incident severity S2 for now. creating follow-up ticket INC-2031-FTW for deeper root cause (cfg hot-reload + flaky network).
priya_ml: cost ticket created: FIN-1248. if we keep >25% traffic on on-demand GPUs >6h we need exec approval.
oncall_j: final status: controlplane stable, auth/routing recovered, serving canary holding at 30% while autoscaler finishes resync. moving to monitoring -> postmortem.
infra-bot: [RESOLVE] incident INC-2031 state=mitigated handler=oncall_j time=1871234900
mike_h: thanks all — please drop logs/notes into INC-2031 and assign owners for network flakiness and config deployment gating.
